issues.evidence: The $47,970 figure is the all-occupation median ('Annual median wage across all occupations is $47,970'). The same Commerce deck puts the Management Occupations median at $124,390. An ACH administrator needs certification: 2 years of college or 60 months of supervisory experience, a 120-hour AIT program and an exam.
issues.fix: Do not price a certified ACH administrator at the all-occupation median. Replace it with a sourced NC OEWS figure for a comparable management occupation, such as 11-9111 Medical and Health Services Managers. That NC figure was not retrieved, so treat it as unverifiable until sourced. Add a payroll-burden line for the administrator, or state that it is an owner's draw. This line drives profit for the ACH configurations.

issues.current: A full-time administrator (40 h/wk) plus aides priced at the CNA median ($18.49/h); no separate Manager position or Manager premium
issues.correct: 10A NCAC 13F .0602 (7–30 residents) and .0606 (7–12 residents): an Administrator or Manager must be in the facility or within 500 ft with two-way communication at all times. A Manager must be 21+, hold a HS diploma/GED, have 6 months of management or supervisory experience (or be a licensed health professional), and earn 12 CE hours a year.
issues.evidence: "There shall be an Administrator or Manager in the facility or within 500 feet of the facility with a means of two-way telecommunication at all times." A 40-hour administrator covers only about 24% of the 168 weekly hours.
issues.fix: Show who is the qualified Manager for the other ~128 hours a week. Either price a Manager at a wage above the CNA median, or state that every 24/7 aide meets 13F .0402 Manager qualifications. The 20-bed models note the 7–12 rule but never mention that .0602 also applies to 13–20 residents. Add a manager-qualification and CE cost line.

issues.current: Cook 40 h/wk and housekeeping 20 h/wk (12-bed); cook 1.5 FTE and housekeeping 1 FTE (20-bed)
issues.correct: The rules require additional staff for daily housekeeping and food service. The designated personal-care staff member may not do food service during the shift, and may do housekeeping only in narrow exceptions.
issues.evidence: "There shall be additional staff to provide daily housekeeping and food service duties." Also: "The staff member assigned shall not perform food service duties during the shift."
issues.fix: A 40 h/wk cook covers about 5 days, and 20 h/wk of housekeeping is under 3 h a day. Add a schedule showing 7-day, 3-meal food-service coverage and daily housekeeping coverage by non-care staff. Otherwise add weekend or relief hours, because this is a compliance risk.

issues.evidence: A competing consumer source for the same state shows "1,808 communities Avg $4,586/mo". The $6,496 CareScout figure sits behind a secondary site (Brevy) that was not retrievable. The Genworth 2024 NC value cited is $5,769. The model's own note says the survey measures a one-bedroom unit in an assisted living community, not a shared room in a small family care home.
issues.fix: Run the 6-bed FCH and 12-bed ACH at a conservative or local private-pay rate, and add a sensitivity case near $4,586–$5,769. Mark $6,496 as unverifiable against primary CareScout data. Every private-pay line scales off this one number, and the break-even and 'net $/month' claims in checklist item 1 inherit it.
